dm: Fools deceived by desire, Thinking, "I must make a living," Enter into battle fearing the loss of life, And for the sake of profit, they go into servitude.
gm: Fools deceived by desires, Wishing for a livelihood and thinking, "I will make a living," Enter into battle despite fearing the loss of their lives, And go into slavery for the sake of profit.

dm: Some who are full of desire even have their bodies mutilated; Some are impaled on the points of stakes; Some are pierced by short spears; And some are even seen being burned.
gm: Some with desires even have their bodies mutilated, Some are impaled on the points of stakes, Some are stabbed with short spears, And some are seen being burned.

dm: Through the torments of accumulating, guarding, and losing, One should understand that wealth is an endless source of ruin. Those who are distracted by their attachment to wealth Have no opportunity to be liberated from the suffering of cyclic existence.
gm: Through the torments of amassing, protecting, and losing it, Wealth should be known as endless ruin. Those who are distracted by attachment to wealth Have no opportunity for liberation from the miseries of existence.

dm: For those possessed by desire, such faults are many and the benefits are few; It is like a beast of burden pulling a cart, That eats only a few mouthfuls of grass.
gm: For those with desires, these and so forth Are the many disadvantages and little benefit, Just like beasts of burden drawing a chariot Eating a few mouthfuls of grass.

dm: For the sake of such a small benefit, which is not even rare for a beast to achieve, Those tormented by their karma destroy This precious human life of leisure and endowment, so difficult to find.
gm: Which is not rare even when accomplished by beasts; For the sake of whatever is that small benefit, This hard-to-find, perfect freedom and endowment Is destroyed by those tormented by karma.

dm: Desires will certainly perish and cause one to fall into the hells and other lower realms; Because it is not for a great purpose, one undergoes constant wearisome toil.
gm: Desires will certainly perish, And they cause one to fall into hell and so forth; For the sake of what is not great, at all times, Whatever fatigue and hardship has occurred,

dm: If Buddhahood could be accomplished with even a millionth part of such hardship, Then for those possessed by desire, compared to the conduct of enlightenment, There is great suffering but no enlightenment.
gm: If by just a ten-millionth fraction of that Hardship, Buddhahood is accomplished, Those with desires have greater suffering than in the Bodhisattva's conduct, And yet they have no awakening.

dm: If one considers the sufferings of the hells and so forth, Even weapons, poison, fire, precipices, And enemies cannot be compared to the objects of desire.
gm: If one considers the sufferings of hell and so forth, For desires, weapons, Poison, fire, precipices, And enemies cannot even serve as examples.

dm: Thus, having become weary of desires, One should generate a delight in solitude, Within peaceful forests That are empty of strife and afflictions.
gm: Having thus generated revulsion for desires, Generate joy for solitude. Empty of disputes and afflictions, In the peaceful forests,

dm: On delightful, expansive stone slabs like palaces, Cooled by the sandalwood-scented moonlight, Fanned by the silent, peaceful forest breeze, One walks about, contemplating the welfare of others.
gm: The fortunate ones, cooled by moonlight and sandalwood, On broad flat stones, delightful mansions, Fanned by the silent, peaceful forest breeze, Pace while contemplating what benefits others.

dm: In empty houses, at the foot of trees, or in caves, Staying wherever and for as long as one desires, Having abandoned the suffering of guarding and possessing, One lives in spacious relaxation, free from attachment.
gm: In empty houses, at the foot of trees, and in caves, Staying wherever and for however long they desire, Having abandoned the suffering of guarding possessions, They live carefree without dependence.

dm: Acting with independence and without attachment, Having no connection with anyone at all, That joy of contentment, whatever it may be, Is difficult even for Indra to find.
gm: Acting independently and without attachment, Unconnected to anyone at all, Whatever is the joyful conduct of contentment, Even Indra has difficulty finding it.

dm: By means of these and other such aspects, Having reflected upon the virtues of solitude, One should completely pacify discursive thoughts, And meditate upon the awakening mind.
gm: Through these and other ways, Having considered the qualities of solitude, With discursive thoughts fully pacified, One should cultivate the awakening mind.

dm: One should first strive to meditate On the equality of oneself and others; Since all are equal in happiness and suffering, One should protect everyone just as one does oneself.
gm: The equality of self and other One should first strive to meditate upon. Since happiness and suffering are equal, All should be protected like oneself.

dm: Just as the body, despite its many different parts like the hands and so forth, Is protected as a single entity, So too are all diverse beings, with their various joys and sorrows, One in their equal desire for happiness, just as I am.
gm: Although the divisions of hands and so forth are many, Just as they are one as a body to be fully protected, Likewise, the different migrating beings, with their happiness and suffering, Are all one in equally desiring happiness, like oneself.

dm: If my own suffering Does not cause harm to the bodies of others, Nevertheless, because I cling to it as "mine," That suffering is unbearable to me.
gm: If my suffering Does not harm the bodies of others, Even so, that suffering is mine, Unbearable due to clinging to self.

dm: Likewise, although the suffering of others Does not fall upon me, Nevertheless, because of attachment to a self, That suffering is difficult to bear.
gm: Likewise, although the sufferings of others Do not fall upon me, Even so, that suffering is mine, Difficult to bear due to clinging to self.

dm: I should dispel the suffering of others Because it is suffering, just like my own; I should benefit others Because they are sentient beings, just like my own body.
gm: I should dispel the suffering of others Because it is suffering, like my own suffering. I should benefit others Because they are sentient beings, like my own body.

dm: Since both myself and others Are equal in desiring happiness, What is so special about me That I strive for my own happiness alone?
gm: When both myself and others Are equal in desiring happiness, What difference is there with myself, That I strive for the happiness of myself alone?

dm: Since both myself and others Are equal in not desiring suffering, What is so special about me That I protect myself and not others?
gm: When both myself and others Are equal in not desiring suffering, What difference is there with myself, That I protect myself and not others?

dm: If I do not protect them Because their suffering does not harm me, Then why protect against future suffering, Since it does not harm me now?
gm: If, because their suffering Does not harm me, I do not protect them, Future suffering also If it does not harm, why protect against it?

dm: The conceptual thought that "I" will experience that Is a mistaken conception, For the one who dies is one, And the one who is born is another.
gm: The thought that "I will experience it" Is a false conception; Thus, the one who dies is another, And the one who is born is another.

dm: If the suffering of any particular person Must be protected against by that person alone, Then since the suffering of the foot is not that of the hand, Why should the hand protect it?
gm: If whenever the suffering of anyone Is to be protected by that one himself, The suffering of the foot is not the hand's, Why should it be protected by it?

dm: If you argue that even if it is illogical, One acts in this way because of grasping at a self, Then whatever is illogical regarding self and others Is precisely what should be abandoned as much as possible.
gm: If you say, "Though it is illogical, here One engages through grasping at self," That which is illogical regarding self and others Is to be abandoned to the best of one's ability.

dm: What are called "continua" and "assemblies" Are false, like garlands, armies, and the like. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Who could be the owner of this?
gm: What are called a continuum and a collection Are false, like a rosary, an army, and so forth. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Therefore, who will have control over this?

dm: Because suffering has no owner, All instances of it are without distinction. Since it is suffering, it must be dispelled; What is the use of making restrictions here?
gm: Since suffering has no owner, All are entirely without distinction. Because it is suffering, it is to be dispelled. What is the use of restriction there?

dm: "Why should the suffering of all be averted?" Is not a point of contention. If it is to be averted, then all of it must be averted; If not, then I am just like other sentient beings.
gm: "Why should the suffering of all Be prevented?" There is no room for debate: If prevented, all should be prevented. If not, I too am like sentient beings.

dm: If you ask, "Since compassion brings about so much suffering, Why should one strive to generate it?" If one contemplates the suffering of the world, How can the suffering of compassion be considered great?
gm: "Since compassion has much suffering, Why forcibly generate it?" If one asks: When one contemplates the suffering of beings, How is the suffering of compassion great?

dm: If by means of a single suffering, A multitude of sufferings can be eliminated, Then those endowed with compassion should certainly Bring about that suffering for themselves and others.
gm: If by a single suffering Many sufferings will be eliminated, The compassionate one should generate that suffering For oneself and others.

dm: Therefore, although Supuṣpacandra Knew of the harm the king would inflict, He did not avert his own suffering, So that the suffering of many might be exhausted.
gm: Therefore, Supuṣpacandra, Even while knowing the king's harm, Did not dispel his own suffering, So that the suffering of many would be exhausted.

dm: Thus, those whose mind-streams are habituated, Finding joy in the pacification of others' suffering, Will plunge even into the Avīci hell Like swans into a lotus pond.
gm: Thus, those whose continuums are accustomed, Because they delight in pacifying others' suffering, Like a swan into a lotus pool, Will plunge even into the Avīci hell.

dm: When sentient beings are liberated, What ocean of joy could be greater? Is that not sufficient in itself? What is the use of desiring liberation for oneself?
gm: When sentient beings are liberated, The ocean of joy that exists— Is that itself not sufficient? What is the use of desiring liberation?

dm: Therefore, even when acting for the benefit of others, There is no conceit or sense of wonder; Because one is single-mindedly devoted to the welfare of others, There is no hope for a ripening result.
gm: Therefore, even when acting for the benefit of others, There is no conceit or amazement. Delighting solely in the benefit of others, There is no hope for a ripened result.

dm: Therefore, just as I protect myself From even the slightest unpleasantness, I should likewise cultivate a protective mind And a heart of compassion toward others.
gm: Therefore, just as to a small degree I protect myself even from unpleasant words, Likewise, a mind of protecting others and A mind of compassion should be cultivated in this way.

dm: Through the power of habituation, One comes to perceive the drops Of another's semen and blood as "I," Even though they are not inherently one's own.
gm: Through habituation, regarding others' Drops of semen and blood, Even though they lack any entity, Just as one apprehends them as "I,"

dm: In the same way, why should the bodies of others Not also be held as "I"? It is not difficult to establish My own body as being other.
gm: Likewise, regarding the bodies of others as well, Why not apprehend them as "I"? Positing my own body as others Is not difficult in that way.

dm: Having recognized oneself as being full of faults And others as an ocean of virtues, One should practice completely discarding self-grasping And adopting others.
gm: Knowing oneself to be flawed, and others To be an ocean of qualities, Completely discarding grasping at self And taking up others should be meditated upon.

dm: Just as the hands and other parts Are accepted as limbs of the body, Why are all embodied beings Not accepted as limbs of the world?
gm: Just as hands and so forth Are accepted as being limbs of the body, Likewise, as limbs of transmigratory beings, Why are embodied beings not accepted?
